about: The 26 approved engagement-first X posts of Nov 23 to Dec 6 (social-posts.md, 'Engagement-first X posts scheduled'), each with the picture made for it. Words are exactly as approved; 'from' says what each picture is made of. Times are WIB, as X's scheduler shows them in this browser.

posts.text: How many tabs are open in Safari on your phone right now? Go and look. I'll go first in the replies.
posts.from: Real iPhone simulator capture (iOS 27.2): Safari's tab overview with nine real pages open.

posts.text: Without looking: what's the last thing you copied on your phone?
posts.from: Real iPhone simulator capture (iOS 27.2): an empty new note in Notes with iOS's Paste menu.

posts.text: What have you typed so many times that your thumbs do it without you? An address, an email, "on my way"?
posts.from: Real iPhone simulator capture (iOS 27.2): Settings > General > Keyboard > Text Replacement, where every iPhone keeps omw for On my way!

posts.text: "Accept all" is one tap. "Reject all" is a second screen, a column of switches and a Save button at the bottom. Somebody sat in a meeting and chose that.
posts.from: Real capture: a large retailer's cookie banner on its US home page at iPhone size, first screen and the screen behind Cookies Settings, cropped below the logo (headless Chrome, 2026-11-23).

posts.text: Mac people: what's the first app you install on a new Mac, before anything else?
posts.from: Real capture: Homebrew's home page, brew.sh (2026-11-23).

posts.text: What's an app you paid for once, years ago, and still open every week?
posts.from: Real photo: the original iPhone, iPhone 3G and iPhone 4 by Yutaka Tsutano, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons; credit on the picture.

posts.text: I pressed the Back button. That was the whole message. Some sites answer it with another page of their own, and then another one.
You can copy on an iPhone by pinching in with three fingers, and paste by pinching out. Does anyone actually use that, or do you still long-press?
posts.from: Real capture: Apple's iPhone User Guide, Select, edit, and move text, the three-finger Cut, Copy and Paste lines (support.apple.com, 2026-11-23).

posts.text: If you moved from Android to iPhone: what's the one thing you still miss?
posts.from: Real screenshot: Android 7.1.2's home screen with Back, Home and Recents, by Google Inc., CC BY 1.0, Wikimedia Commons; credit on the picture.

posts.text:
Black Friday, Nov 27 to 30 on the App Store:
Cutling $2.99 (was $4.99)
Undirect $0.99 (was $1.99)
One purchase covers iPhone, iPad and Mac.
posts.from: The two sale cards made on 2026-11-20 (social/sale-cutling-ig.png, sale-undirect-ig.png): each app's real icon and a real screen of the app, with the sale prices.

posts.text: Paste. "Allow Paste". Paste again. "Allow Paste". It's my phone and my clipboard. Who else would it be?
iPhone people: are you on Apple's keyboard or another one? What made you switch, or stay?
posts.from: Real iPhone simulator capture (iOS 27.2): the keyboard list iOS shows when you hold the globe key.

posts.text: Korean writes "tap" and "tab" the same way: 탭. So my App Store headline about pop-ups that hijack your taps now says 터치, touch. App makers: which word of yours looked fine until it was translated?
posts.from: Real: Undirect's first Korean App Store screenshot before commit 03202520 and now (Support/AppStore/ko/iphone/01.png), top part.

posts.text: Apple rejected my app twice in one week for the same thing: my App Store preview videos showed a phone around the screen. A preview may only use captures of the app itself. Has that one caught anybody else?
posts.from: Real: a frame of Cutling 1.6.1's rejected iPhone preview (cutling-promo/out/preview/preview-iphone-en.mp4, 1.2 s) beside guideline 2.3.4 on Apple's App Review Guidelines page.

posts.text: Apple doesn't publish how much memory an iPhone gives a keyboard. It's in the firmware: 77 MB. A share sheet gets 120, a widget 30. Go over it and iOS shuts the keyboard. Keyboard makers: what did you have to cut to fit?
posts.from: Real capture: the firmware table in Cutling's docs/research/keyboard-memory-limits.md on GitHub (2026-11-23).

posts.text: People who make apps alone: how many languages is yours in, and who checks the ones you can't read?
posts.from: Real capture: the Languages row of Undirect's App Store page, opened (apps.apple.com, 2026-11-23).

posts.text: In May I capped a snippet at 1,000 characters. I thought the keyboard's memory was why. My own commit says "because of iOS form layout issues". The next version takes 10,000. What limit did you set for a reason you've since forgotten?
posts.from: Real capture: Cutling commit 0e7878b on GitHub, its message and its CutlingStore.swift change (2026-11-23).

posts.text: What's the oldest app still on your home screen, and why has it survived?
posts.from: Real image: the first iPhone's home screen, iPhone OS 1, by Avicente05, CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons; credit on the picture.

posts.text: My app is in 50 languages, and no native speaker has read any of them yet. If you read something other than English: what's the first thing that tells you an app's translation was never read by a person?
posts.from: Real: Undirect's first App Store screenshot as it ships in Arabic, Hindi, Tamil, Thai, Hebrew, Japanese, Russian and Greek (Support/AppStore/<locale>/iphone/01.png).

posts.text: Apple rejected my first iPhone submission, and they were right. My setup button said "Open Safari Settings" and opened the wrong page, so the reviewer got stuck on the first screen. App makers: which rejection can you laugh about now?
posts.from: Real screenshot: Undirect's setup screen as submitted in September (docs/screenshots/iphone-setup.png), cropped around the button.

posts.text: Would you pay for an app whose code is public, when you could build it yourself for free?
posts.from: Real captures: Undirect's App Store page ($1.99) above its public GitHub repository (GPL-3.0), both at phone width (2026-11-23).

posts.text: Mac people: what's the first thing you delete when you set up a new Mac?
posts.from: Real icons: eighteen of the apps every Mac ships with, exported from this Mac's /System/Applications by NSWorkspace (macOS 27.0.1), with their names.

posts.text: I opened one article and got a newsletter box, a cookie banner and an "Open in app" bar before I could read the first sentence.
Solo makers: how do you decide a bug is bad enough to fix today, and not in the next release?
posts.from: Real capture: the Expedited reviews section of Apple's App Review page (developer.apple.com/distribute/app-review, 2026-11-23).

posts.text: What's a Safari behaviour that still surprises you?
posts.from: Real iPhone simulator capture (iOS 27.2): Settings > Apps > Safari > Close Tabs, where Safari can close tabs by itself after a day, a week or a month.

posts.text: The hard part of stopping tabs a page opens by itself is telling "the person tapped this" from "the page did this while they were looking at something else". Safari extension makers: which signal do you trust?
posts.from: Real capture: lines 733 to 748 of Undirect's guard.js on GitHub, the navigate handler that decides whether a person pressed (2026-11-23).
